This operation produced large amounts of cuttings at the shakers but was not considered to be directly pressure related but was rather due to the generation of swelling gumbo clays from approximately 1300m down to 1600m. Below 1600m the hole conditions appeared to be more stable with little resistance during the trip and it was from this depth that the resi

rom the three treatments are studied to assess the clay mineral assemblages present. Peak height measurements are taken and incorporated in Carver analysis to quantify the amounts of clay minerals present. To assess the amount of swelling clay present (i.e. Smectites) the ethylene glycol solvated trace is studied together with the heated trace. The untreated trace is used to quantify the amounts of non-swelling phase
